question: When we eat something we like, our mouth waters by a fluid called saliva. In this situation, which enzymes break starch into simple sugar?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Amylase enzymes**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Amylase enzymes** are responsible for breaking down starch into simple sugars, such as maltose and glucose.
 
• Amylase is present in human saliva and initiates the process of digestion in the mouth.
 
• The enzyme is also produced by the pancreas and secreted into the small intestine.
 
• There are two main types of amylase: **salivary amylase** (produced in the salivary glands) and **pancreatic amylase** (produced in the pancreas).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Saliva Composition:** Saliva consists of water, electrolytes, mucus, and enzymes like amylase which begin the digestion of carbohydrates.
 
• **Role of Amylase:** Amylase breaks down complex carbohydrates into simpler sugars which can be easily absorbed by the body.
 
• **Digestion Process:** The digestion of food starts in the mouth with the mechanical action of chewing and the chemical action of enzymes such as amylase.
 
• **Pancreatic Amylase:** Apart from salivary amylase, the pancreas secretes pancreatic amylase into the small intestine to continue the digestion of carbohydrates.
 
• **Enzyme Specificity:** Different enzymes are specific to different macronutrients: amylase for carbohydrates, proteases (like pepsin) for proteins, and lipases for fats.
